title: Global Terrorist Organizations
subtitle: Exposing False Agendas and Human Rights Violations Worldwide
introPara1: This comprehensive documentation exposes terrorist organizations operating globally under false religious and political agendas. These groups systematically violate human rights, commit mass atrocities, and destabilize entire regions while claiming to fight for justice or religious causes.
introPara2: From the rise and fall of ISIS to ongoing operations of Hamas, Taliban, and regional groups like PFI, these organizations share common tactics: exploitation of vulnerable populations, religious radicalization, targeting civilians, oppression of women, and recruitment of child soldiers.
introPara3: This page provides detailed information about banned organizations (like ISIS, Al-Qaeda, Boko Haram, PFI), currently active groups (Hamas, Hezbollah, Taliban, Al-Shabaab), and regional threats across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Each entry documents their false agendas, actual crimes, and impact on human rights.
warningText: This page contains detailed documentation of terrorist activities, mass atrocities, and human rights violations. Content may be disturbing. All information is sourced from international security agencies, UN reports, and verified news sources.
org1Aka: Also Known As: Islamic State, ISIL, Daesh, Islamic State of Iraq and Syria
org1Location: Iraq, Syria (formerly controlled territory spanning 34,000 sq miles)
org1Desc: ISIS emerged in 2014 claiming to establish an Islamic caliphate. Under the false agenda of creating a pure Islamic state, they committed genocide against Yazidis, mass executions, enslavement of women, and destruction of cultural heritage. Declared their caliphate in June 2014, controlled territory until 2019. Responsible for over 33,000 deaths and displacing millions.
org1Crimes: Genocide against Yazidis, Christians, and Shia Muslims (UN-documented)
Sexual slavery of 6,800+ women and girls (UN Human Rights Council)
Mass executions and beheadings broadcast globally
Recruitment and use of 1,500+ child soldiers
Destruction of UNESCO World Heritage sites (Palmyra, ancient Mosul)
Chemical weapons use against civilians (chlorine, mustard gas)
org2Location: Afghanistan, Pakistan, Yemen, Somalia, North Africa
org2Desc: Founded in 1988 by Osama bin Laden, Al-Qaeda claims to fight against Western influence in Muslim lands. Their false jihad narrative masks global terrorism, including the September 11, 2001 attacks killing 2,977 people. Responsible for bombings in Kenya, Tanzania, USS Cole, Madrid, London, and countless other attacks. Operates through affiliated groups worldwide.
org2Crimes: USS Cole bombing: 17 US Navy sailors killed (2000)
Continuous suicide bombings killing thousands of civilians
org3Aka: Western Education is Forbidden, Jama'atu Ahlis Sunna Lidda'awati wal-Jihad
org3Location: Nigeria (Borno, Yobe, Adamawa), Cameroon, Niger, Chad
org3Desc: Founded in 2002, Boko Haram opposes Western education and seeks to establish Sharia law. Their campaign of terror has killed 350,000+ people and displaced 3 million in West Africa. Gained global attention by kidnapping 276 Chibok schoolgirls in 2014. Pledged allegiance to ISIS in 2015.
org3Crimes: Kidnapping of 276 Chibok schoolgirls (2014), 110 still missing
3 million displaced persons, 2.5 million need humanitarian aid
Systematic rape and forced marriages of abducted women
Bombing of churches, mosques, markets, and villages
org4Aka: Islamic Resistance Movement, حركة المقاومة الإسلامية
org4Status: Active (Designated terrorist by US, EU, Israel, Canada)
org4Desc: Founded in 1987, Hamas claims to resist Israeli occupation but uses terrorism against civilians. Governs Gaza since 2007, launching thousands of rockets at Israeli cities. The October 7, 2023 attack killed 1,200+ Israelis and took 240 hostages, triggering major conflict. Rejects Israel's right to exist and uses Gaza civilians as human shields.
org4Crimes: 15,000+ rockets fired at Israeli civilians since 2005
Suicide bombings killing hundreds during Second Intifada
Using hospitals, schools, mosques as weapons storage (UN documented)
Human shields: placing military installations in civilian areas
Execution of political opponents in Gaza
Building terror tunnels using aid money meant for civilians
org5Status: Active (Designated terrorist by US, UK, Arab League)
org5Desc: Founded in 1985 and backed by Iran, Hezbollah operates as both a political party and terror organization. Maintains large arsenal of 150,000+ rockets aimed at Israel. Participated in Syrian civil war supporting Assad regime. Designated terrorist organization for attacks including 1983 Beirut barracks bombing killing 241 US personnel and 58 French soldiers.
org5Crimes: Beirut barracks bombing: 241 US, 58 French personnel killed (1983)
Syrian civil war participation: supporting Assad's war crimes
Drug trafficking in Latin America funding operations
Assassination of Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik Hariri (2005)
org6Status: Active (De facto rulers of Afghanistan since 2021)
org6Desc: Ruled Afghanistan 1996-2001 and retook control in August 2021. Implements extreme interpretation of Sharia law, including total ban on girls' education beyond 6th grade. Provided safe haven to Al-Qaeda before 9/11. Despite promises of moderation, continues severe oppression of women, public executions, and harboring terrorist groups.
org6Crimes: Complete ban on girls' education above grade 6 (1.4 million girls affected)
Women banned from work, public spaces, universities
Public executions and floggings resumed since 2021
Mass killings of civilians in Mazar-i-Sharif, Bamiyan
Forced marriages and systematic oppression of women
org7Status: Active (Designated terrorist by US, UK, UN)
org7Desc: Emerged in 2006 from Islamic Courts Union, pledged allegiance to Al-Qaeda in 2012. Controls parts of southern Somalia despite African Union forces. Known for brutal enforcement of Sharia, banning music, sports, and aid organizations. Launched major attacks in Kenya including Westgate Mall (2013) and Garissa University (2015).
org7Crimes: Garissa University attack: 148 deaths, mostly students (2015)
Banning humanitarian aid causing famine deaths
Assassination of Somali politicians and journalists
org8Aka: Popular Front of India, Campus Front of India (CFI)
org8Location: India (Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh)
org8Desc: Founded in 2006, PFI claimed to work for social justice for minorities but operated as radicalization network. Indian government banned PFI in 2022 under UAPA for anti-national activities, funding terrorism, and promoting enmity. National Investigation Agency (NIA) documented connections to ISIS, forced conversions, and planning violence against Hindu activists and politicians.
org8Crimes: Radicalization and recruitment for ISIS (NIA documented cases)
Murder of Hindu activists: RSS/BJP workers in Kerala, Karnataka
Plans to establish Islamic rule by 2047 (seized documents)
Training camps for violent activities in Kerala forests
Funding through hawala and foreign sources (₹1,000 crore traced)
Love jihad cases: forced conversions after marriage (multiple FIRs)
org9Aka: JeM, Army of Mohammed, جيش محمد
org9Status: Active (Banned by UN, US, India, UK)
org9Desc: Founded in 2000 by Masood Azhar (released in IC-814 hijacking), JeM focuses on attacks in India, particularly Kashmir. Responsible for 2001 Indian Parliament attack, 2016 Pathankot airbase attack, and 2019 Pulwama attack killing 40 Indian soldiers. Operates training camps in Pakistan with ISI support. Designated global terrorist organization.
org9Crimes: Pathankot airbase attack: 7 security personnel killed (2016)
Suicide bombings in Jammu & Kashmir killing hundreds
Infiltration and cross-border terrorism from Pakistan
Recruitment and radicalization of youth in Kashmir
org10Aka: LeT, Army of the Pure, لشکر طیبہ
org10Status: Active (Banned by UN, US, India, UK, EU)
org10Desc: Founded in 1990 by Hafiz Saeed, LeT operates from Pakistan targeting India. Responsible for 2008 Mumbai attacks killing 166 people over three days. Despite ban, operates openly in Pakistan as Jamaat-ud-Dawa (JuD). Extensive training infrastructure and funding network. Focuses on Kashmir and attacks across India.
org10Crimes: Operates training camps producing hundreds of militants
org11Aka: Al-Qaeda in Yemen, تنظيم القاعدة في جزيرة العرب
org11Desc: Formed in 2009 by merger of Al-Qaeda branches in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Considered one of most dangerous Al-Qaeda franchises. Published Inspire magazine encouraging global attacks. Behind numerous plots including 2009 underwear bomber, 2010 cargo plane bombs, and Charlie Hebdo attack inspiration. Controls territory in Yemen's civil war.
org11Crimes: Charlie Hebdo attack: 12 deaths in Paris (2015)
Cargo plane bomb plot targeting US (2010)
USS Cole bombing: 17 US sailors killed (2000)
Publishing Inspire magazine promoting global jihad
Controlling Yemeni territory and imposing harsh Sharia
org12Aka: Bearer of the Sword, جماعة أبو سياف
org12Status: Active (Designated terrorist by US, Philippines, Australia)
org12Desc: Founded in 1991, Abu Sayyaf is the most violent terrorist group in Philippines. Known for kidnappings, beheadings, and bombings. Pledged allegiance to ISIS in 2014. Finances operations through ransom kidnappings of foreigners and locals. Despite military operations, continues attacks in southern Philippines.
org12Crimes: Kidnapping of over 600 people since 1991 (many beheaded)
Beheading of Western hostages and posting videos
org13Aka: HuJI, Movement of Islamic Holy War
org13Status: Active (Banned by Bangladesh, India, US, UK)
org13Desc: Founded in 1984 in Afghanistan, HuJI spread to Bangladesh, Pakistan, and India. Active in terrorist attacks in Bangladesh and India. Known for targeting secular intellectuals, religious minorities, and Indian targets. Operates training camps and has links to Al-Qaeda and Taliban. Implicated in multiple bombings and assassination attempts.
org13Crimes: Assassination attempts on Bangladeshi PM Sheikh Hasina
Targeting of secular bloggers and intellectuals in Bangladesh
Training camps for militants in Bangladesh-Myanmar border
Collaboration with other terror groups (JMB, LeT)
Bomb attacks on Hindu temples and Christian churches
conclusionTitle: Critical Analysis: The Reality Behind False Agendas
conclusionList: Common Pattern: All these organizations claim religious justification while systematically violating Islamic principles against killing innocents, oppressing women, and destroying property.
Women & Children Most Affected: Sexual slavery, forced marriages, denial of education, kidnappings, and use of child soldiers are consistent tactics across all groups.
False Jihad Narrative: These groups pervert the concept of jihad to justify mass murder, terrorism, and criminal activities including drug trafficking and extortion.
Economic Devastation: Terrorism costs the global economy over $1 trillion annually through direct damage, security costs, and lost productivity.
Refugee Crisis: Terrorist activities have displaced over 80 million people globally, creating the worst refugee crisis since World War II.
Regional Instability: Organizations like ISIS, Taliban, and Boko Haram have destroyed state institutions, education systems, and healthcare infrastructure.
Radicalization Machinery: Groups use sophisticated propaganda, social media, and educational institutions to recruit vulnerable youth worldwide.
Financial Networks: Despite bans, these organizations maintain complex funding through illegal activities, foreign sponsorship, and exploitation of charitable donations.
International Response: UN, US, EU, and regional powers have designated these groups as terrorists, but enforcement remains challenging due to safe havens and state sponsorship.

Human Rights Catastrophe: Combined, these organizations are responsible for millions of deaths, sexual violence against hundreds of thousands, destruction of cultural heritage, and systematic human rights violations affecting entire regions.
